# Repository Guidelines

## Project Overview

Qortoo is a Rust SDK for conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) with distributed synchronization. It provides atomic transactions with rollback, read-only observation modes, and pluggable connectivity backends.

## Critical Guidelines

- **English**: Write code comments and shared, tracked documentation in English. Personal plans under `qortoo-harness/.local/plans/` use the user's session language.
- **Design**: Favor SOLID principles, especially SRP and OCP; check them during review.
- **Tooling Ownership**: Keep shared Claude/Codex tooling in `qortoo-harness`. Other repositories carry only their root `AGENTS.md`; do not add `CLAUDE.md` or tracked `.claude/settings.json`. Personal, gitignored agent state is local.
- **Worktrees**: Create isolated worktrees outside every repository, under `../qortoo-worktrees/` relative to the harness. See `qortoo-harness/docs/repository-hygiene.md`.
- **Personal Work**: Keep all plans in `qortoo-harness/.local/plans/` and task lists, working notes, and logs under its `.local/`. Never commit personal `.local/` or `.claude/` state. Update the plan's status, checklist, and progress log during the work, including corrections and scope decisions.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Use emoji + conventional messages with a specific package/module scope: `🧬feat(scope): summary`, `🪲fix(scope): summary`, `📜docs(scope): summary`, `💿CI/CD(scope): summary`, `🧩chore(scope): summary`, `🧪test(scope): summary`, `⚡perf(scope): summary`. See `/qortoo-shared:commit` for the full table.
- Target PRs at `main` and squash-merge; the PR title/body becomes the final commit message. Include a concise summary, testing commands, and issue links where applicable. See `/qortoo-shared:pr`.
- When behavior changes, update docs and add or adjust tests.

## Documentation Guidelines

- Qortoo is unreleased: document current intended behavior and principles, without intermediate development history or migration notes unless the user requests history. Add compatibility/migration guidance only for released behavior.
- Organize concept documentation under `./docs/`, with Markdown and diagrams grounded in the code. Use `/qortoo-shared:doc-new` to scaffold concepts.

## Personal Plan Lifecycle

- Keep active plans in `qortoo-harness/.local/plans/`.
- Before closing a plan, verify its checklist and external delivery state. Keep it active while any acceptance condition remains.
- Mark a finished plan complete, record its final outcome, and move it to `qortoo-harness/.local/archive/`. Retain completed plans; never commit either directory.

## Project Structure & Module Organization
- `src/` holds the Rust crate, with modules like `clients/`, `connectivity/`, `datatypes/`, `errors/`, `observability/`, `operations/`, `types/`, and `utils/`, plus shared roots like `constants.rs` and `defaults.rs`.
- `tests/` contains integration tests (e.g., `tests/datatype_builder.rs`, `tests/datatype_handler.rs`, `tests/metrics.rs`).
- `examples/observability/` contains runnable trace, log, metrics, and profiling examples.
- `qortoo-ffi/` owns the C ABI, generated header, native SDK metadata, and ABI tests.
- `docs/` contains the full architecture documentation — see [Architecture](#architecture) below.
- `qortoo-rs-docker/` contains the local observability stack configuration.
- `coverage/` is generated by `cargo tarpaulin` and is not source-controlled.
- Root files of note: `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `.rustfmt.toml`, and `Makefile`.

## Rust Toolchain
- **Edition**: 2024
- **Minimum Rust version**: 1.87.0
- **Nightly required** for `rustfmt` (used in `make lint`)

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the full command reference — it runs with
only `cargo`, `make`, and `git`, no agent or plugin required. `make doc` has an
agent-only variant, `/qortoo-rust:doc-generate`, that adds a missing-doc report.

## Architecture

The full architecture is documented in `docs/`, kept accurate via `/qortoo-rust:doc-review` (staleness/coverage check) and scaffolded via `/qortoo-shared:doc-new <concept>`. See [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) for the complete index; the core documents are:

- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — layer stack, shared state model, operation flow, and concurrency model (including thread-safety rules: `Arc<RwLock<T>>` for shared mutable state, all public datatype types are `Send + Sync`)
- [`docs/client-and-datatype-builder.md`](docs/client-and-datatype-builder.md) — `Client`, `DatatypeBuilder`, and where naming validation runs
- [`docs/datatype-state.md`](docs/datatype-state.md) — `DatatypeState` lifecycle and write-access rules
- [`docs/transaction-and-rollback.md`](docs/transaction-and-rollback.md) — `TxRecord`, transaction lifecycle, inverse-operation rollback, `OperationId` semantics
- [`docs/connectivity.md`](docs/connectivity.md) — `Connectivity` trait, `NullConnectivity`, `LocalConnectivity`/`LocalDatatypeServer`, `WiredInterceptor`
- [`docs/handler-system.md`](docs/handler-system.md) — `DatatypeHandler`, `HandlersManager`, priority-based async dispatch
- [`docs/event-loop.md`](docs/event-loop.md) — priority-based event processing, channel types, exponential backoff behavior
- [`docs/error-handling.md`](docs/error-handling.md) — error taxonomy, `RecoveryAction` routing, sync-path vs commit-path recovery
- [`docs/observability.md`](docs/observability.md) — feature flags (`observability-log` / `-trace` / `-metrics` / umbrella), managed setup, local stack (`make obs-up`)
- [`docs/go-binding.md`](docs/go-binding.md) — `qortoo-ffi` C ABI, ownership rules, error mapping, header generation, and native SDK staging
- [`docs/performance.md`](docs/performance.md) — central Rust/Go latency benchmarks and results owned by `qortoo-bench`

When you change behavior described in one of these documents, update it in the same change — don't let `AGENTS.md` or `docs/` drift from the code (this happened before: this file used to duplicate `DatatypeState`'s variant names inline and had gone stale relative to `src/types/datatype.rs`; the fix was deleting the duplicate and linking to `docs/datatype-state.md` instead).

## Testing Guidelines
- Name test functions `can_<behavior>` (e.g. `can_reject_a_null_collection`), describing the
  behavior being proven rather than the code path under test — consistent across unit and
  integration tests in this repo.
- Use `cargo test` for unit/integration tests; async tests use `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = N)]`.
- Test macros: `get_test_collection_name!()`, `get_test_func_name!()` for unique names; `new_attribute!(DataType::Counter)` and `new_client_common!()` for unit-level construction.
- Parametric tests use `rstest`; polling assertions use `awaitility`.
- Prefer `#[instrument]` on tests that need tracing.
- **`LocalConnectivity` realtime pitfall**: call `connectivity.set_realtime(false)` before creating datatypes when you need deterministic test ordering (e.g., to register a handler before the first auto-sync fires).
- **`qortoo-ffi` test scope**: before writing a test under `qortoo-ffi/tests/` or `qortoo-ffi/src/`, ask "if the C ABI were deleted and this called the safe Rust API directly, would it still make sense as a `qortoo-rs` test?" If yes, it belongs in `qortoo-rs`, not `qortoo-ffi` — CRDT correctness, state-machine transitions, and sync semantics are the core's responsibility to prove, not the boundary's. Keep `qortoo-ffi` tests scoped to what only exists at the boundary: null-pointer/invalid-UTF-8 handling, ownership (exactly-once free/userdata-drop), Rust-error-to-i32 code mapping, and callback-trampoline marshalling. When a test needs the counter in a particular state, treat that as minimal setup, not the thing under test — don't re-derive multi-client sync or CRDT value propagation to prove a pointer argument works. Also apply this within `qortoo-ffi` itself: if another test in the same crate already exercises a call as incidental setup, or already proves the same fact more strongly, a dedicated smoke test for it adds no signal.
- **`qortoo-ffi` completeness signal**: don't use `make ffi-coverage`'s line-coverage percentage as a target to hit (it isn't a CI gate). Most of `qortoo-ffi` is thin pass-through wrappers, so a coverage percentage rewards filler tests over real boundary coverage. Judge completeness by the explicit contract checklist instead — every exported symbol exercised, every null/invalid-UTF-8/ownership/error-code case asserted — and treat an uncovered line as worth investigating only if it's a case that checklist actually calls for.
- **Cross-datatype test duplication**: when adding a new datatype (e.g., `Variable` alongside `Counter`), don't copy a sibling datatype's test for shared, datatype-agnostic plumbing — `DatatypeBuilder` key validation, readonly enforcement, lifecycle-state gating — onto the new one just because it has its own `build_*` method. That plumbing is proven once, by whichever datatype's test exercises it first; a second copy re-tests the same shared code path under a different name and adds no signal. Write a new datatype's own tests for what actually differs: its CRDT semantics, its value contract, and that its builder method actually constructs and wires up that concrete type.

## Naming Validation

Collection names and datatype keys follow different rules, and both lengths are measured in
bytes. [`docs/client-and-datatype-builder.md`](docs/client-and-datatype-builder.md) owns those
rules, with accepted and rejected examples and the point each one is checked. Do not restate
them here or in another document.

Use `/qortoo-rust:doc-review` to check all docs for staleness and missing coverage. Use `/qortoo-shared:doc-new <concept>` to scaffold a new concept document. See [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) for the full documentation index.

qortoo-rs specific: CI enforces coverage with an 80% minimum, while local `make tarpaulin` enforces 90%.
